content.title: Nebraska women’s basketball falls to Baylor in NCAA first round
content.text: Nebraska women’s basketball (19-13) fell to Baylor (25-8) on Friday in a first-round matchup of the NCAA Tournament. The Bears won 67-62 inside Cameron Indoor Stadium in Durham, North Carolina, and will stay there to play No. 3 seed Duke on Sunday in the second round. This is the sixth year in a row Baylor has advanced past the first round, and the fifth under head coach Nicki Collen. “What a game,” Collen said. “I guess this is what the NCAA Tournament is all about. We got tough at the end, and when time was running out, I thought that was about the toughest five minutes we’ve ever played.”As for the Huskers, this is the second year in a row they have lost in the first round and the fourth time in total for head coach Amy Williams. Nebraska is now 10-18 in March Madness contests.“This is tough,” Williams said. “It’s always really tough when your season comes to a close. This is a team that I’m very proud of how they fought through the sunshine and storms that come with a season. They showed great character through all of that.”Despite not securing the upset, Williams and the Huskers will come home with a First Four win under their belt and plenty of hope for the future. Here are three takeaways from Friday’s round of 64 matchup:Baylor defends the paint and holds onto lead for most of the first halfThe Huskers have lived by the 3-ball all season, and that strategy was carried out yet again in the big dance. However, they were also forced to take a lot of shots from behind the arc, 21 to be exact, because of the Bears’ ability to steer away any attack at their own basket. Nebraska made nine of those 3-point shot attempts and continued to let it fly from deep once Baylor locked down the Husker frontcourt. The Bears led for most of the first half due to their aggressive defense, but they weren’t able to consistently pull away on offense. Sophomore guard Yuting Deng led at the half with six points, senior forward Bella Fontleroy had five and three Bears had four points each. It took some time for them to pull away in the second half, but they were doing it to a better degree in the first because of some shooting troubles for Nebraska.Prince struggles from the field in first halfSophomore guard Britt Prince did not score until just under the six-minute mark in the second quarter, and even then, it was only a pair of free throws that got her on the board. Heading into the first round, she led the team with 17.6 points per game, but was initially quiet from the field. It was instead junior guard Logan Nissley who took charge at first, picking up 11 points off of 4-for-10 shooting and making three of her four 3-point attempts in the first half.Of course, though, with a minute left in the second quarter, Prince hit her first field goal of the game to give Nebraska its first lead. She went 1-for-6 from the field in the first half, with four of those being 3-point attempts. Prince opened the second half with another 3-pointer and didn’t look back after that. She finished with 27 points off of 8-for-19 shooting and knocked down all eight of her free throw attempts. The Huskers may have lost, but Prince’s second half offensive resurgence sure made this game a close one. “I want to lay it all out on the line for my teammates,” Prince said. “I love them and love playing with them. We all wish the outcome was different, but we fought hard out there and laid it all out on the line for each other."Both defenses tighten up to make second half a nail-biterWhile Prince was able to turn things around shooting-wise, Baylor’s leading scorer Taliah Scott was not. Scott, a redshirt sophomore guard, went into Friday averaging 20 points a game, but was only able to put up two in the first half against the Huskers.Scott shot 3-for-12 from the field, missing all eight of her 3-point attempts. However, she did go 9-for-12 at the free throw line and led the team in points with 15. Due to Scott’s struggles from the field and Nebraska guarding the paint more efficiently, Baylor was unable to pull away in the third, and the game stayed within two scores for the entire second half. With 3:48 left in the fourth, a flagrant 1 foul was assessed to junior forward Jessica Petrie for her fourth personal of the game. On the following play, Petrie fouled again, leading to her fouling out and Nebraska playing without their most versatile forward for the final three and a half minutes of the game. Petrie had 10 points before fouling out.The Bears made three of those four free throws off of Petrie’s fouls which gave them their first lead since Prince hit that 3-pointer before halftime. Despite a valiant effort from Prince and sophomore forward Amiah Hargrove, who had six points and 11 rebounds, the Bears never lost the lead after getting it back late in the fourth. Baylor won 67-62 and will play No. 3 seed Duke on Sunday, while Nebraska ends its 2025-26 campaign with a 19-13 overall record. sports@dailynebraskan.com
